newsitem.title: NORWAY: Elkem Q1 profits hit by lower prices.
newsitem.headline: Elkem Q1 profits hit by lower prices.

text.p: Norwegian metals producer Elkem ASA said on Monday that a 24 percent slump in first quarter profits year-on-year was mainly due to a decline in prices in all its markets.
But it said it expected demand for products to remain on the same level as in 1996.
The company booked pre-tax profits of 237 million crowns ($33.6 million), down from 312 million crowns in the first three months a year ago, but up 29 million crowns from the fourth quarter 1996.
Operating profits fell to 261 million crowns versus 343 million crowns.
"Compared to the fourth quarter of 1996, the development in results in the first quarter of 1997 was positive for the manganese/chrome business, and for aluminium," Elkem said in a statement.
"Compared to the first quarter of 1996, ferrosilicon, manganese/chrome and aluminium all recorded a decline, mainly due to lower prices in the respective markets."
Operating profits in the ferrosilicon sector dropped 26 percent to 75 million crowns against 101 million crowns in the first quarter 1996.
Elkem said steel production in the western world was four percent higher than in the year-ago period, with the increase particularly strong in Asia and Western Europe.

"By and large, demand for ferroalloys is still good. Average prices for ferrosilicon, measured in Norwegian crowns, were nevertheless somewhat lower than in the fourth quarter 1996," the company said.

In the manganese and chrome division operating profits tumbled to 29 million crowns from 106 million crowns. Elkem said ferrochrome prices were steady from the fourth quarter but average levels for manganese alloys were somewhat lower.
Profits at the group's material division were stable at 80 million crowns against 85 million crowns, while aluminium dropped 36 percent to 28 million crowns.
Elkem said aluminium prices had improved substantially in the first three months compared with the final quarter last year, in particularly for products in the transport and building sectors.
